title: personal-llm-mini-experiment-tracker
content:
Mini experiment tracking sheet (personal) - quick reference and notes

CSV-style rows for quick copy/paste into a real sheet:

Experiment ID,Model,Quant,Batch,Temp,Prompt V,Input Subset,Tokens per req,Avg Latency (ms),Cost / 1k tok,Metric,Metric value,Notes
exp-001,redwood-small,8-bit,8,0.7,prompt-v1,subset-A,420,85,$0.035,exact-match,0.62,fast but some repetition; baseline for subset-A
exp-002,redwood-small,4-bit,8,0.7,prompt-v1,subset-A,420,78,$0.028,exact-match,0.60,slightly worse EM; occasional decoding artifacts
exp-003,redwood-medium,4-bit,4,0.3,prompt-v2,subset-B,1200,210,$0.12,ROUGE-L,0.48,better coherence; higher latency/cost
exp-004,open-7b,fp16,8,0.5,prompt-v2,subset-A,360,95,$0.05,exact-match,0.57,good quality/cost tradeoff
exp-005,redwood-medium,8-bit,16,0.7,prompt-v1,subset-C,220,70,$0.09,exact-match,0.55,batching improves throughput; watch tail latency

Quick notes:
- Baseline: exp-001 for subset-A (prompt-v1). Use as reference for regression checks.
- Prompt-v2 includes clarifying instruction for hallucination reduction; works better on subset-B for coherence.
- Quantization: 4-bit gives small EM drop but significant cost/latency savings; watch for occasional token-level artifacts.
- Batching: increases throughput but adds tail latency; consider adaptive batching for production.

Immediate next runs (short):
- exp-006: redwood-small,4-bit,prompt-v1.1 (few-shot 2 examples), subset-A, temp=0.5 -> compare EM and hallucination count
- exp-007: redwood-medium,4-bit,prompt-v2,subset-B, temp=0.3 -> measure ROUGE-L and latency under 95th pct load

TODO (personal):
- Add automated eval script (python) to compute exact-match, ROUGE-L across subsets and output CSV
- Hook this mini-sheet to quick slack report (daily) for errant regressions
- Add cost-normalized metric column (metric / cost) for easier comparison

Scratch shorthand (notes to self):
- "few-shot" = include 2 examples inline; check token budget
- "subset-A" = small task set (50 examples, short prompts)
- "subset-B" = longer form summaries (20 examples)
- "subset-C" = edge-case queries (30 examples)

Links: CONFLUENCE-LLM-PROMPTS-221 (prompt bank), GH-PR-845 (eval script WIP), LINEAR-312 (experiment infra task)

Status: draft - this is my working mini-sheet for ad-hoc runs and quick comparisons.
